Subject: PoC / Trial - Success Criteria & KPIs (latency / throughput / cost / quality) - Atlas Payments

Hi Priya / Sanjay —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call to keep momentum on the PoC planning. Please review and flag anything missing.

Goals discussed:
- Validate Redwood inference for real-time authorization workflows (transaction scoring) at Atlas scale
- Measure latency and throughput under representative traffic patterns
- Confirm unit economics (cost / token) and model quality relative to your acceptance criteria

Proposed success criteria / KPIs (first pass):
1) Latency: p95 end-to-end generation latency <= 200ms for typical requests (payloads ~80 tokens)
2) Throughput: sustained throughput of 50 requests/sec with burst capacity to 150 req/sec without p95 degradation beyond 20%
3) Cost / token: target effective model cost <= $0.0008 / token (including batching and caching benefits)
4) Quality: >= 95% correct classification on the provided evaluation set and no regression vs. your baseline model on the top-5 loss cases
5) Availability: maintain availability >= 99.9% during test window

Evaluation plan (high level):
- Week 0: Exchange datasets, SOW, and sandbox access (we share a short SOW + evaluation plan)
- Week 1: Deployment of trial environment (dedicated pool) + baseline runs using your sample traffic
- Week 2: Stress testing and latency/throughput sweeps; cost projection runs
- Week 3: Quality evaluation on held-out set; joint review and recommendation

Ownership / roles:
- Atlas: provide evaluation dataset, expected traffic profile, SLA constraints, and decision owner (Priya to confirm)
- Redwood: set up trial environment, run sweeps, share dashboards and cost breakdowns (Marissa will lead ops)

Next steps / asks (for this week):
1) Priya — confirm decision owner and preferred trial window (dates)
2) Atlas — share a representative sample of traffic (anonymized) + evaluation sample (CSV)
3) Redwood — we will send the PoC SOW and a detailed evaluation plan by EOD today (attachments)

Attachments: Atlas_PoC_SOW_v1.pdf, PoC_Evaluation_Plan.xlsx (draft)

Thanks — happy to sync if you want to walk through the plan live.

Best,
Jordan

Thanks — looping in the ops details from my side. A few clarifications and what we'll deliver: 

Deliverables from Redwood for the trial:
- Provisioned dedicated trial pool (NVIDIA A100 x4 equivalent) with access credentials and runbook
- Dashboard with p50/p95 latency, throughput (req/s), token counts, and cost breakdown per model/route
- Automated sweep scripts to ramp traffic and capture tail latency and memory usage
- Cost projection spreadsheet for hosted vs dedicated (we'll include assumptions)

Clarifications / proposed adjustments to KPIs:
- Latency: propose p95 <= 250ms as a practical target for the first run; we expect to optimize to <= 200ms once we tune batching and KV cache settings. If Atlas needs strict 200ms p95 for go/no-go, call that out as a hard acceptance criterion.
- Throughput: confirm whether the 50 req/s target is steady-state or peak. We suggest defining steady-state 50 req/s and peak 150 req/s for short windows.

I'll attach the evaluation plan draft and the SOW to the shared drive and send a signed SOW template once Priya confirms the window.
